statement_en: Let $a_n:=(-1)^n$. Then its partial sums are $$S_n:=\begin{cases}1&n\text{ is even}\\0&n\text{ is odd}\end{cases}$$ so $S_n$ does not converge. However, this sequence is Cesaro summable, because $$\sigma_N:=\frac{S_0+\cdots+S_{N-1}}{N}=\frac{\lfloor\frac{N}{2}+1\rfloor}{N}$$ and its limit is $\frac{1}{2}$.

import Mathlib
open scoped BigOperators

def a (n : ℕ) : ℝ := (-1 : ℝ) ^ n

def S (n : ℕ) : ℝ := Finset.sum (Finset.range (n + 1)) a

def sigma (N : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  if h : N = 0 then
    0
  else
    Finset.sum (Finset.range N) S / (N : ℝ)

theorem alternatingSequenceCesaroSummable :
    (∀ n : ℕ, S n = if Even n then 1 else 0) ∧
    (¬ ∃ l : ℝ, Filter.Tendsto S Filter.atTop (Filter.nhds l)) ∧
    (∀ N : ℕ, N ≠ 0 → sigma N = ((Int.floor ((N : ℝ) / 2 + 1) : ℝ) / (N : ℝ))) ∧
    Filter.Tendsto sigma Filter.atTop (Filter.nhds (1 / 2 : ℝ)) := by
